review_text: Right across the street from Independence Hall, Red Owl Tavern is a must-try for those in Old City Philly. It has a rustic and charming feel in the dining areas, and servers were quite friendly. My compatriots and I all enjoyed our meals, which were reasonably priced. I had the BLTB, which is your classic three-pronged sandwich along with Brie cheese. It was irresistible. We were there at the time of day when both breakfast and lunch were offered, so making a final decision on what to have was difficult, in a good way. Red Owl soars above in regard to food presentation and quality of taste. Owl surely be coming back sometime!

This was one of the best meals I had during the 4 years I went to school in Philly.  I saved it for my senior year, and it was well worth the wait.  The service was impeccable, and the food itself was amazing.  I was temporarily overwhelmed by the variety and couldn't decide if I wanted to take the sweet or savory brunch route.  Luckily the buffet setup allows you to do a little of both.

The place was a little more quiet and formal than I'm usually comfortable with, but who cares when you have such a great brunch spread before you?

Called and placed an order for take out. We ordered a small pizza and baked ziti. They told us it would take 30 mins. We got there in 35 mins and it was all still in the oven so we had to wait. 

The pizza was really good. I would definitely get it again but it was that good that I would crave it. It was very greasy which I didn't like. 

The baked ziti only had cheese on the top so once that first layer was eaten it was honestly just red sauce and noodles. They definitely should put more cheese through the ziti.

Came here for brunch - loved the shakshuka and cheese curds! I got one of the pouch drinks which I wasn't crazy about but it's fun and worth getting it. The mimosa was good too. I came in the winter in one of their outdoor booths, I really wish it was a little more spacious and kept more warm (it was freezing.) I'd be back in warmer weather or if I were able to get an indoor reservation!

The restaurant is beautiful, cute and rustic. Unfortunately the food was terrible. I ordered a grains and eggs and my girlfriend got an avocado toast. Both our meals tasted like adding seasoning would cost the kitchen staff their job. Like really is it that difficult to prepare an meal that has flavor. 

Bottom line our meals tasted like boiled water. Other than that I love atmosphere.

Had a great time sitting at the bar and having dinner. The bartender was friendly and attentive. Food was above average for pub food. My wife enjoyed the Impossible Burger with bacon, because why not have meat and not meat too! Will be back!
Very disappointed in quality. Meat was partly raw in soup dumplings. None of the food was hot... Everything was slightly cooler than room temp. Spoons and plates all had some leftover stains on them.
Wonderful food and it tasted very fresh.  The food definitely stood out as the place wasn't all that charming.

I really like the food here. Extremely fast delivery and good service anytime I've order. However, nothing is ever really flavorful or seasoned very well. I literally have to go home and add seasonings to whatever I buy because the flavor is so bland. So strange. But once again, the food is well made and fresh. So hey. Win some lose some.

I've dined here now over ten times...in groups, with one or two close friends, and on a date night.  The one thing that is consistent about this place is that the quality of food completely fluctuates.  I've had dishes I've loved but more often I've had dishes where I leave thinking I could definitely make this at home and way better.

If you're going to dine here, stick to salads, apps and small plates.  The entrees are extremely disappointing - over-sauced; dried out meat; under-seasoned; soggy, un-fresh vegetables.

On a side note the friendliness of the staff also fluctuates. I've come when they've been so lovely and nice and have even given us complimentary dessert and other times when they're rude and tell us that there's a reservation and they need our table 30 minutes after we have sat down.  Note to staff:  a smile and a nice greeting  goes a long way.

They have a wide menu but the quality was pretty terrible on everything we ordered. They also made some mistakes on a couple of the items, and their customer service about fixing these mistakes was subpar.

Somebody else already said it: you're not going to be impressed with this place. I'll just list some words that describe it below.

1) Mundane
2) Bad service
3) Lame menu

The food just isn't good. I recommend avoiding this place. You'll be disappointed; or at best full, but not pleased.

Our experience started out good, a nice table outside looking out at the bridge. We first enjoyed a delicious bowl of muscles and were content that our meals would be the same, but we were sadly wrong. The worst part was the extremely overcooked and dry shrimp kabobs, which I would highly recommend not getting. The soft crab was unappetizing and not worthy of being called a "special". The rest of the food (gnocchi and scallops)  had no specific problems but was Hardly average.

I knew I should have just driven my ass to Chinatown!

I decided to order take out from this place which is kinda in my neighborhood.   The menu was pretty decent, lots of the typical run of the mill Americanized selections.

I got the szechuan chicken, with an egg roll and wonton soup.  Pretty standard huh?  Well that's what I was hoping.  But nope....let's just say I was very unsatisfied with the quality and had to go out and get something else to eat.  To me it was that bad.  

First of all the eggroll was the greasiest little sucker, which wouldn't have been that bad if it was actually tasty.  The wonton soup had the worst tasting broth and very 'unusual tasting' wontons in it.  Mystery meat?  Who knows.  At least cover it up with some spices or something.  It was bland to say the least.  The szechuan chicken was blah to the extreme.

Finally our order came and we took off for home immediately to enjoy food since we were starving.  Now typically when I'm starving,  anything tastes delicious but not today. The meat was undercooked and chewy and the dumplings had portions undercooked which we had to spit out from our mouth.
I've been to Dim Sim garden several times and usually it has met my expectations but not today. It was very disappointing and this seems to be the trend since our last dine-in experience was not great either.
I really hope they improve and bring back the old quality of food & service back.

Went for lunch. Service was worth 4-5 stars, but the meat--the highlight of the meal--was sub-par.

The salad bar was good, but not great. Everything's made to look pleasing, but the vegetables were primarily undercooked. Nothing was incredibly flavorful.

The meat was hit or miss between four of us at the table. The worst, by far, was the filet mignon. It was so tough and chewy that we couldn't finish more than one bite. Aside from the cuts of meat not being good quality, the flavors were bland.

Another disappointment was that only a handful of the meat options from the menu were walked around. We were told there were lamb chops, but never saw or had them come to the table.

Just as disappointing was that half the time we had no idea what was being served. We were repeatedly told "sirloin," but there are THREE cuts of sirloin on the menu. Which was it? We'll never know.

We started off with the bruschetta w/ shrimp and empanadas.  The bruschetta looked great but had absolutely no flavor and I was actually pretty grossed out by it by the third bite.  The chicken empanada was the highlight of the meal.  It was delicious!

Then the entrees came out.  The steak was ridiculously fatty.  Had to cut off and discard huge parts of it.  The pasta w/ seafood was bad.  Room temperature and super bland.  Again, absolutely no flavor to anything.  Very disappointed in these costly entrees.

The ambiance is ok, nothing special.  Food was pricy and extremely bland (except for the chicken empanada).  Service and drinks were fine.  Disappointed in the overall experience because we were really looking forward to it.

This place is not that good. I tried like the food here but the noodles weren't that tasty and the broth was actually extra bland. They gave us promotional skewers and meat had a strong stinky smell to it. It was weird. Overall I did not have a pleasant time with the food.

I get to a shrimp in the Jatujak that is right on the line of undercooked. I figured with the temperature hotness of the food it is probably fine, dumb mistake. The next day I was writhing in stomach pain.

Like I said before, they were busy, the chef even had to come out to help a little (which is an admirable trait for someone in the kitchen), but ignoring a table for 45 minutes when all they wanted was some more water (yes we did ask) and then serving undercooked seafood due to the pressure of getting the food out is inexcusable. 

On paper the food looked amazing, but on my plate and in my stomach it disappointed. There is plenty of other delicious Thai Food in that area the I will stick with.

Flavors were very good. Food was delivered, not eaten at the restaurant. Everything tastes very good. However, each of the dishes was sweet. That is an unusual flavor for the cuisine, so it stood out. Overall, great experience.

I'm curious if this particular restaurant doesn't inspire the kindest clientele, because she appeared visibly shocked when I asked her how her evening was going.

Our food came out relatively quickly, which was great! If I had to choose one word to describe the food it would be "overcooked". I will give them a lot of credit for the unique flavor combinations that we experienced - some of the rice dishes in particular stand out. Anticipating fresh, bright flavors, we leaned heavily toward the seafood side of things, which may have been a mistake. Shrimp were well overdone and tasteless - the kind you might expect if you make the mistake of ordering shrimp fried rice from a Chinese restaurant that is clearly a front for something less legal. The cebiche itself was tough and chewy, but the accompaniments were tasty.

Something about the food has changed within the last year.  We eat here periodically, and last night the food was very bland.  My wife had 2 slices of pizza which lacked flavor and I had a mini sausage boli which also lacked flavor.  The onion rings we had were very over cooked and again, lacked flavor.  

The food used to be much better.  Maybe the management changed suppliers, but whatever the reason behind the bland food it's bad.  I doubt we'll be returning.

I ordered a bunch of dim sum dishes from here a week ago and when I say it was a disappointment, I mean it was a MAJOR disappointment. The chicken feet I ordered was not only not prepared correctly, it was under-cooked! The starch was not cooked, the chicken was cold -- it was disappointing. I also ordered rice rolls (which were cold and under-cooked), rice rolls w shrimp (under-cooked), shrimp har gow (...you guessed it: undercooked! You're starting to see the theme here, right??), siu mai (cold and pork was under-cooked so I threw it out. Not tryna die over under-cooked siu mai pork!! The only thing that turned out right were the spring rolls -__- 

I've been missing dim sum like crazy and when I finally had the opportunity to order some...I was left with a big mess of under-cooked disappointment.

I dont know what happened to this place.
The food is bad. Thats all i can say. 
Not once or twice a bad meal but 4x
I like the atmosphere but the food is bland and tastes old! 
Sorry! 
Too many stomach aches

Service was fine and accommodating, but the food was just totally bland and uninspired. There were five of us, and we ordered a variety of dishes ranging from pasta to risotto to veal. No one was impressed.

The veal had little taste or seasoning. The seafood didn't seem fresh. The pasta doesn't come across as freshly made, and the risotto was under cooked.

If you've ever had true, great Italian food, you will likely find this restaurant stuffy and lackluster.
The food was pretty bland. I had the veggie combo and nothing really stood out except one stewed carrot that was delicious. The service was so slow too.

So far it's 3,5** in my book but it has potential. 
We've been in their NY location once couple yrs ago. Can't say we liked our experience their.
But reading lot's of positive reviews about this location we thought we'd give them another try.
It was much better experience then in NY, but still had some flows.
  POSITIVE:  Ambiance (clean, nicely decorated, accompanied with soft pleasurable music background), Service (attentive, friendly). Some of the dishes we've tasted were very yummy  (Stuffed eggplant, Shrimp Chive Dumplings) and not overly greasy as the other Philly dim sum places offer.
  NEGATIVE: Maybe because we were the first customers at 10:30am and they were not quite ready in the kitchen, but unfortunately not all of the food was tasty or for that matter freshly cooked.

Shocked and saddened by just how disappointing this place was.  After reading such great reviews, my girlfriend and I walked in with such high expectations.  By the end of the meal we were wondering if we had done something wrong.  We just didn't get what all the fuss is about.  For starters, the place is far from cozy.  Feels like you're sitting in a cafeteria.  We decided to start the evening with a refreshing cocktail and we went with the highly touted Lemonnana.  A so-so drink that wasn't very lemony, wasn't very minty, wasn't very anything.  Appetizers, we ordered two hummus dishes and they were tasty and, little did we know, would be the highlight of the meal.  From the small plates menu, I went with the chicken soup, BLAND, and the calf tongue, BLAND!  To finish, I decided to try Beef Cheeks for the first time.  Tender and meaty but, you guessed it, BLAND.  COMPLETELY TASTELESS.

The interior is very pleasant, with a calm yet buzzingly sociable atmosphere.  My dining companion and I had the tasting menu.  The salatim ranged from fabulous (fennel, carrots, eggplant...) to oddly flavorless (tabouleh, cucumber).  The bread, in small supply, was delicious, as was the traditional, smooth hummus.  The cauliflower with labni was fantastic.  The lamb sausage and lamb kefta were great.  The smoked chicken was excellent.  The service was very good.  My cocktail was superb.  Desert was very good.  Overall, I"m a little torn because I really liked it there, but my primary complaint was that the portions were much too small for even tapas style.  For having had the entire tasting menu plus drinks and desert we left not even remotely full and wound up eating again later.  Had the portions been better sized I would say it was worth the price tag.
Great fresh and authentic food! I didn't expect it to be so delicious, or for the presentation to be so impressive.

Finally 2 of our breakfasts arrived after making the rounds to all the tables nearby.  We awkwardly sat waiting for our last person to be served while our food got cold.   Finally we all had our food and were willing to put the horrendous service behind us for a delicious meal.  Wrong again...  the food was barely edible.    Disgusting would be a better term for it.  Drenched in oil, undercooked and flavorless.... just awful.  We poured on the hot sauce hoping to add some taste but finally just gave up.     We were so disappointed and certainly would never go back to this place again.  Besides the decor there is truly nothing good to say about it.

The food was amazing, the service could've been a bit better for sure. Our waiter wasn't very attentive or friendly at the least. However, other staff in the restaurant were very helpful and friendly.
Good food but truly awful delivery from this location.

Right across the street from Independence Hall, Red Owl Tavern is a must-try for those in Old City Philly. It has a rustic and charming feel in the dining areas, and servers were quite friendly. My compatriots and I all enjoyed our meals, which were reasonably priced. I had the BLTB, which is your classic three-pronged sandwich along with Brie cheese. It was irresistible. We were there at the time of day when both breakfast and lunch were offered, so making a final decision on what to have was difficult, in a good way. Red Owl soars above in regard to food presentation and quality of taste. Owl surely be coming back sometime!

I love this restaurant, their food is beyond good BUT - they have the rudest staff I have encountered in a long time. They stood at the front desk complaining about people who come for happy hour (sorry for giving you business). The waiter took a happy hour menu away from us before we were done.  He then took our food and boxed it without asking if we were finished. Finally he brought our check without asking, returned twice in five minutes to pick it up (we all still had full glasses of wine), acted annoyed, and continued to push us to leave even though we weren't done. I have come here for years, but this has happened three times in a row - and I may be done.

I forgot. To say the staff is VERY RUDE..  They look upon customers as a bother. And feel they can serve up this Slop and you should be greatful.hurry up and pay and get the hell out. Politeness and customer service is Not in there Skillset..Also they dont cook there steaks to order . They have this huge pile of precooked meat. They scoop up the meat slap it on the roll they laddle on the liquid cheese. Yummy. Are you hungry yet.. Disgusting

TERRIBLE CUSTOMER SERVICE. The hostess was beyond lazy and rude. The staff were slow and incompetent. Please hire people that actually want to work and not these lazy people that have no regards to the customers.

Horrible experience and horrible food. The staff was very rude, standoffish and disinterested to an extreme. The hostess's demeanor was unfriendly if not outright hostile. The waiter was rushing us through the whole dining experience. I felt like we were at a fast food joint. Within two minutes of sitting us he wanted to know what we wanted to drink and to eat. After asking him to give us a couple of extra minutes, he made a face and appearead annoyed. We felt very uncomfortable with our waiter. He came back in two minutes, ignored the fact that my husband was on the phone, and interrupted him during his business calll as we wanted to know if we were ready to order. That was no more than 5 minutes into him sitting us and us trying to get comfortable! My husband had to hang up and place the order. We ordered a meatball appetizer, two shitty spaghetti dishes and garlic bread.

Have eaten here a few times but felt the need to write this review after my most recent visit when I was completely let down by the service. Yes, the food is great but it's accompanied by some of the worst attitudes of any Center City restaurant I've visited. The host and servers create an atmosphere where they seem to be defending some food and beer utopia that customers are intruders upon or worse yet -- unworthy of. The hosts are usually rude if not downright nasty and grumpy, while the servers are lackluster at best. 

I ordered the excellent and delicious burger but without the sweet potato fries that come with it. Of course that's exactly what I got. Later on in our meal it took the server about 25 minutes to ask us if we'd like another drink. Lastly, when we split the bill he choose to remind us to tip on the original amount. I'm pretty sure that's unnecessary no matter what.

Staff is just really unfriendly and unkind. It's a common experience not only I have had but have also heard from others. They are just plain rude to their customers. I'm really surprised that management doesn't seem to care at all to fix this, or maybe that's the vibe they're going for.

My sister and I came to this restaurant for the first time tonight and we will never be coming back. The staff is nothing but rude and disrespectful. We waited nearly 20 minutes for someone to come and take our order. Our waitress, Bryanne, was very kind but every other staff member left a bad taste in our mouths. The hostess/busgirl was by far the WORST. She was a shorter heavier set older Caucasian woman with a black bob. I do not know her name but I do know that her attitude and customer service is absolutely awful. I went to the bathroom at one point (which was disgusting to say the least) and was walking back to my table and I so happened to be following behind the hostess. She saw me following her and snapped at me saying "can I help you?" in the rudest manner.

Their food is below average, but their service is the worst I've ever experienced in the entire city!!!
Rude, ungracious staff.
Food was late, cold and incorrect.
They did nothing to correct

Nice food and venue but the staff member was extremely rude and judgemental. I'm not someone to complain but she was looking at us like we had 2 heads and were aliens. The staff member expected us to know exactly what they had instead of answering our question. There was no line or anyone behind us yet she was unwilling to answer 1 basic question about what flavors they have. Sadly I will not want to come back here due solely to how unwelcome we were treated. Management please contact me.
The service is really bad. We couldn't get waited on, so we walked out. The waiter was too busy talking to his friends.

My husband and I came here on a Sunday night around 7 PM, and it was pretty busy. 

The hostess at the front was timid, and didn't give off a welcoming vibe. We didn't really have any place to sit or stand, so we decided to wait around by the cashier or take out stand. The woman behind there was even worse - no acknowledgement, and she had her head down. Not sure if she was a supervisor or manager. 

We waited about 30 minutes to get seated, and the family in front of us was skipped. We both wondered why a party who arrived later than we did was sat down first, so we both headed towards the host.

I don't write Yelp reviews often so I'm sure this will get buried as most of them seem to, but we had an annoying experience at DoubleKnot yesterday and felt that it should be shared so people avoid the same fate.  We had a reservation for 2 people at 8:15PM and arrived pretty much on the dot.  We went to check in with the hostess who took our information and asked us to get a drink at the bar while they make our table ready.  At around 8:40 we started staring at our watches.  By 9PM we were getting hungry.  My wife went to ask the hostess how much longer we might expect the wait to be and were met with a very rude response.  She told us (with a good deal of attitude) that she wasn't sure when our table would be ready, wasn't sure how many people were in front of us, and wasn't sure when or if we'd be able to eat.

Please do something about your staff that has attitude and is aloof almost every time i come in. There have been some amazing and wonderful staff that are professional and warm however there is a young girl that has a terrible attitude who has rolled her eyes at me and made it difficult to ask for anything with my sandwich. It has happened multiple times and I always let it go because you never know what someone is going through but it's become too consistent to not say anything at this point. Today she straight up ignored me while looking at me in the face when it was my turn to order. It ruins my experience and doesn't make me want to come in anymore.  I love your food but for the price i expect better customer service. I work in customer service myself and have been for over 15 years. I would not tolerate staff treating customers in that manner.

While I have been here before and had a great time, I cannot say the same for today. When I walked in late this afternoon I stood by the hostess stand for a few minutes, and when no one came over to seat me I assumed it was a seat yourself deal. I took a seat in one of the booths and waited for a few minutes. Nothing. I'm a server myself and could see the staff was busy so I didn't mind the few minute wait. We've all been there. A few more minutes went by and still nothing. A young couple then sat in the booth behind me and was quickly greeted by a server, who noticed me sitting, no settings, no drink, no menus, and did nothing. A minute later, another couple came in and was quickly greeted. At this point I was there for 17 minutes and had not been acknowledged by anyone. I even tried to wave one of the servers over and just nothing.

Went in to grab a slice with my co-workers at lunch. We had the worst customer service experience ever. The women behind the counter didn't offer to help us , didn't acknowledge anything. We spent 20 mins trying to get a slice. Not worth it
Food is amazing. Staff are so rude, impatient, and unfriendly. They rolled their eyes at us multiple times, snatched the menus out of our hands, and were incredibly curt

There are just a few airport bars I really like, and this is (close to being) one of them.

Jet Rock has many positives - chief among them being the draft beer selection: 48 quality pulls, skewing heavily towards the ales.  Whiskey (or whisky, depending upon your potable preference) lovers will appreciate choosing from among 19 single malts and blends.

Don't like draft?  Fear not, they have two bottled beers as well, 

The bar itself, a grand sweeping behemoth studded with fluorescing ceramic and brass draft-towers, is the central eyepiece in this concourse.  The wall is lined with a few high-tops, and a mawing cavern awaits those to be seated at a traditional 4-top.  This area, while truly an image of purgatory for any agoraphobics out there, at least offers a view of the tarmac.  wow.

The staff is rude, plain and simple. They don't know what customer service is or even common courtesy. Food is good but like I said, as a group they have no idea what they're doing or how to talk to people. Go elsewhere if you can.
I like the food, when you finally get seated. Unfortunately, the staff is RUDE, RUDE, RUDE. They need to clean house and hire personel that treat the customers with respect.

While the food is tasty, the staff is extremely rude and confrontational.  I saw them get in an argument with the woman in front of me (the cashier argued over and over again that the woman had ordered one thing, not the other) and then they gave me attitude when I requested brown rice over white.  They also gave the guy behind me a hard time.  Management needs to get engaged in this front end - it's really not an appropriate way to run a business.

As a college student, I love Banana Leaf. It can be rowdy at times but it's always a good time. We tend to go in a group with a few boxes of wine (BYOB). It's not uncommon for the restaurant to be loud with college kids, which can be good or bad. Our group doesn't mind as we are also loud college kids.

The menu is pretty large and there will be something for everyone in your party. Start with the Roti Canai. It's delicious, the "bread" itself has a good texture and the sauce they serve it with compliments it very well. When I went yesterday, I had the Captain's Noodles with flat noodles. It was pretty good. I've also had their spicy chicken, curry chicken, and pad Thai. There are a ton more things on the menu that I would like to try. Also, the fried ice cream is good. Everything on the menu is extremely affordable.

I live in the neighborhood and have been to Soy Cafe quite a number of times over the past couple of years.  I mean, yeah, I'll probably go back, mostly for the convenience.  Their menu has a lot of variety, especially for a healthy-diet kind of restaurant.  Their sandwiches and wraps are all pretty delicious, albeit pretty overpriced for what they are, and serving sizes leave a lot to be desired.  I mean, really, is throwing an extra handful of veggies on that rice paper that cost you $0.01 but you're charging extra on top of the sandwich price for, really hurting your bottom line?

The smoothies are hit-or-miss, sometimes made with way too much ice which makes them slushy and flavorless, but usually pretty delicious, I'd say 7/10 visits.  Most seem to be around $6.00, which I think is still overpriced, but fair for the area.
Except for the extraordinary long wait time, it was great food. Most of the staff is extremely friendly and helpful, there is one, who I presume is the boss and/or owner who is very rude.
Not to pile on, but I also had to comment about the poor service: slow, confused and unfriendly.

We asked for two extra chairs to accommodate the party, and she appeared inconvenienced to give chairs for her diners.  The bathroom needed attention.   We paid almost $700 for the meal for the party.  M&S's owner should be ashamed to give people such poor service!  Beware of this place, go elsewhere!
The food is so wonderful, truly the best I've ever had, but the staff is inattentive and borderline rude.
Poor service even when it's not busy. Staff wasn't attentive and food came out after a very long wait

So it doesn't take much from you to be more courteous and friendly, more than that great service = great tips!
- beef carpaccio was delicious but I didn't like the veal escalope. It was heavy, not fully cooked, and tasteless.
- really wanted a dessert but after poor service we decided to finish our dinner. 
- I understand it is a busy place but if you smile it will elevate everyone's mood around you.

If we decide to visit this place again I hope it will be better.

I really wanted to love this place but the service was terrible. Our server forgot 3 out of the 9 dishes we ordered. We even had to ask for dessert menu and he forgot to bring that out for us. He wasn't attentive at all. We even told the managers about our experience and they didn't seem to care. The food was good but the service ruined it for me. Would of expected better service for the price. Hope you have better luck than me!

Went with a friend who highly recommended this restaurant.  The food was delicious, but the service was terrible - the polar opposite of attentive. We waited about 20 minutes after being seated before a waiter came over.  We waited at least 20 minutes after we were (obviously) finished eating, and finally had to get up and find someone to ask for our check.  Ridiculous.  The restaurant was not especially busy. My friend has been many times and said the service was never like this, but she didn't know any of the staff, which surprised her - maybe they just hired a bunch of new people.  I would try it again, just because the food was excellent, but if the service is this bad every time, I can't recommend the place.

This is probably one of the best places in the neighborhood. It has friendly staff and pretty good food. In fact, I don't think I've had anything I didn't like. (Except the coconut shrimp which clearly were not cleaned before cooking - ick!)  Unfortunately, the service sucks. 

The first few times I went here the service was average - I didn't have to wait exceptionally long for anything. Lately, it seems like the staff just forgets they have people in the dining room. I might understand if the restaurant were full but it never is. So why do I have 10 minutes for someone to come greet me after I've been seated, another 5 for some water, and another 5 to order food? And this is on a regular basis! At least seat me with the menu to speed up the process.
Also the staff is very welcoming and attentive!
Lastly, the staff is friendly, welcoming and attentive.
Staff was friendly, knowledgable, and attentive without being overbearing. Our waitress gave great recommendations and asked for feedback. All in all, it was a great experience!

I wouldn't say the staff was "friendly" but they were attentive and efficient, which I actually prefer over someone friendly and incompetent. Overall it was a good experience and I'm sure I will be going back in the future.

I went on restaurant week to Chima with two of my friends. While the waiters carrying the cuts of meat were excellent and very attentive, our two actual waiters provided very poor service. Not only did they never check on us during our meal, but we waited over an hour for someone to come over with our check. Once we were ready to pay, we waited another 45 mins for the waiter to get our friend's credit card. We then waited over an hour for our waiter to come back with the credit card. They were impossible to flag down, as they totally avoided eye contact with us. Granted, I know they were busy during restaurant week, the service was nevertheless inexcusable. Chances are, I'll never come here again due to the service.

Food is quite good. 
Very reasonable prices.
Nuff said.

I ordered a fiesta cheesesteak and took it to Wissahickon Brewing Company.  The fiesta Cheesesteak lived up to its name, there was a party going on in that roll.  The fiesta cheesesteak had fried onions, mushrooms, green peppers, pepperoni and sauce.  Was it a party in that roll or a train wreck?  The only flavor that really stood out was of a canned mushroom. In my humble opinion, when you have that much stuff together it needs to spend time on the grill together cooking and blending and mixing flavor so you have some kind of uniform taste.  The good news is it was big and we were at Wissahickon Brewing Company.  I had at least two beers and they were all (maybe had more than 2) very flavorful and good.

Came here for brunch - loved the shakshuka and cheese curds! I got one of the pouch drinks which I wasn't crazy about but it's fun and worth getting it. The mimosa was good too. I came in the winter in one of their outdoor booths, I really wish it was a little more spacious and kept more warm (it was freezing.) I'd be back in warmer weather or if I were able to get an indoor reservation!
Excellent for the $$. Obviously not the best, but the prices are very very reasonable. The venue is small ~10 people and byob, which is perfect for intimate meal.

Expensive.  It was good, but it wasn't so amazing that it should have cost quite so much.  We split our meal and even our salad, so that made it very reasonable.  That made the meal MUCH, MUCH more enjoyable.  We will definitely come back.

Taste: 7/10
Price: 9.3/10

$9.99 for this lunch special (I got nachos on the left and Sopes on the right)

Food was aight. The free chips (top row) were good tbh they were a little thicker than normal chips and a little more cooked so they were all super crispy and addicting to eat; HOWEVER that green dipping sauce for the chips was like dipping it in water lol come on dont do em like that 

The NACHOS were on point the chips were all crispy still plus them beans and chorizo chunks and peppers and cheese was some mmm mmm mmmm i like me some loaded nachos that arent soggy well done there

I got a Sopes because i had no clue what it was. TBH this was my first time eating an avocado in my life LOL it was actually pretty good tbh idk about paying $2 for an avocado over getting like a donut but again id needa experiment more with them. The sopes itself was ehhhhhhhhhhhh.

The food was ok, not great not bad. The service was fine. The prices are far too high for what you get. At least one of three things needs to change: the prices (down) , the food quality (up to amazing), or the quantity of food for the price (portions are small). Right now the price/quantity mix is just out of whack.
Food is good. But for the price they charge the portions are small and not what I expected for the price taste wise.

I wanted to update my review, since my latest experience here blew me out of the water.  Everything from start to finish was perfect.  It helped that we got sat in the beautiful outdoor patio area by the garden with the strung lights - very romantic.

Our server was extremely knowledgeable about the wine and helped us pick what to get based on our personal preferences/food choices.  

As for food, last time I visited was in October and the menu has completely changed since then, which means it rotates seasonally and that's always a nice plus.

To start, we split the lamb skewers appetizer.  Adorable presentation and the meat was so juicy and flavorful, it practically fell off the skewers.  Spicy dipping sauce was dope.  Homemade warm bread and olive oil for the table is also still delicious.

My boyfriend and I stumbled upon this place and decided to give it a try. In terms of food and service, it was great. I loved how afterwards I didn't feel that gross, full feeling. I felt like the meal was light, senseable, and overall healthy. 

My biggest issue with the meal however is the price. Just went for a simple lunch, ended up costing almost $50 dollars. These prices are a little ridiculous and they really need to consider reducing the price. Remember, Ramen Bar, you're in UNIVERSITY CITY catering to poor college students, NOT Rittenhouse Square!!

OVERRATED!! It was expensive and not even that good. Dinner for two of us was $200 and we ordered one drink each and no dessert. Speaking of dessert, the options were meh. We ended up going somewhere else to get dessert that night. We ordered about 5 plates and ended up really liking only one of them. It absolutely wasn't worth the high price tag. Save your money and go somewhere else.
I thought this was kind of overrated.  Food was alright but I thought that it was not worth the price

The food was very overpriced. Tried to sit in the lower down restaurant area as I have bad joints and cant sit on stools and got told that wasnt allowed if I was ordering from the bar. The food is very overpriced for what it is. The waiters are very rude and not at all helpful. They made me feel like I was a hindrance and I spent the whole time there wishing i went elsewhere for dinner. 

There are many more places in the area with better service and more reasonably priced food. It was not worth the stress it gave me for the expense it ended up being.

Most of the food items were very good, but some of them were very average and just not worth the price. If money is not an issue, this is a good place to try. Otherwise, make sure you stick to a few great menu items or you will be disappointed. I'll start with the items I thought were very good. I really enjoyed the Albondigas (Lamb Meatballs,Shaved Manchego), Ensalda de Jamon (Serrano Ham & Fig Salad,
Cabrales, Spiced Almonds), Alcachofas y Setas (Artichokes,
Wild Mushrooms, Black Truffles Manchego Flatbread) Gambas al Ajillo
(Garlic Shrimp), and Alcachofas a la Parmesana
(Parmesan Artichokes), The Manchego Pasamontes
(Truffled Lavender Honey) was unique, but the portion was very small.  The Patatas Bravas (Spicy Potatoes) were bland. The Chorizo was very chewy, and all I tasted was salt. The Scallops were average at best, and you get two scallops cut in half (so four pieces) for $26.

What did I just spend $250 dollars on? The overall meal and service was good but definitely not worth the price. The apps and sides were good but the steaks tasted like something I could have bought at Costco.

I would rate this place 3.5 stars.

Came here for lunch and I gotta say that the mojitos are soo good but way too strong for me (I can't handle anything, my husband had it).  They make them with pure sugar cane juice which makes them extra good, but they don't come cheap. I think it was about $13 for the mojito. 

We started off with the fire and ice ceviche which was good but really tiny.  It was quite expensive as well. I think about $15. Not worth the price.

I ordered the Plato Miramar salad which was: house smoked tuna, mojito-cured salmon, smoked duck breast, Serrano ham, queso blanco, sweet grape tomatoes, caper berries and marinated asparagus. Watercress and romaine salad, Spanish sherry vinaigrette.  This salad was good but a bit too salty because of all the meats and the caper berries. 

My husband ordered the good ole EL Cubano sandwich. The sandwich was delicious.

Every detail shines through here, from the classically and beautifully styled rooms, tables and bars to a simple brunch meal. The beer list is well curated and the fact you can get a 20oz pour of your top choice ( I went with the Prima Pils) adds a little extra joy. 

A great place for dinner with the parents or to celebrate a special occasion, or even just because sometimes you want a big beer and a classic English breakfast. 

I chose a sausage egg and cheese with triple fried chips. Not health food by any means but so good you'll happily loosen your belt. The bread is buttery and a little crispy, with great flavor in the meat and satisfying texture from the gooey cheese and an egg that runs ever so slightly. The fries were thick, but crispy and we'll seasoned. Dessert and coffee satisfied, though I can't say it excelled. 

Staff and service are strong, cool without being aloof.

This place is way overpriced and definitely lacking in their portions sizes for the prices of their entrees. The step down dining, is something I like. It's a slightly dark place. The lighting from the small track lights above do just enough illumination. It reminds me of a reformed wine cellar. The booths are tall, yet you sit at ground level. All around you are those scientific artist renderings of various species of seafood. Be that as it may, I wasn't impressed. Where as with Lacroix, I was treated to something special. This was kind of normal, average. I digress. I really love their complementary biscuit, served with sweet butter cream. More please! For our appetizer we had the small order of Muscles in garlic butter juice. I love seafood and Muscles especially. There was enough for the both of us and it came with a nice size of (Sourdough?) garlic bread.

The service was pretty bad. They placed us towards the back when there were plenty of tables in the middle area where we would want to sit. They said they were 'reserved' but nobody sat in those tables the whole 2.5 hours we were there. So we were right next to the kitchen and bathrooms. Plus the table right behind us they placed a homeless woman there that spilled everything everywhere. It was horrible for the price we paid to eat there. The waitress took forever to give us the check after we said no to desserts. 

We're a minority so it makes me think that they were racist somehow and placed us all the way towards the back when there's clearly tables in the middle. 

All in all service was horrible, food was a little too pricey for the service they gave us and sitting us next to a homeless lady with all her bags.

Beware of portion sizes and always ask for prices.I've been to this location for a late dinner with friends. Great decor and atmosphere.

Food quality is good but definitely not worth the price. The three of us all got something different and we all needed to get more food somewhere else after leaving even though we paid the same as we would for full sized entrees at other area eateries. 

A friend asked for a cheap wine recommendation and got hit with a bill for a $15 glass of wine. Yikes! Always ask of prices when a recommendation is offered.
Portions weren't as big as I was expecting for the food was tasty. A little overpriced for that size of the plate.
It wasn't the worst food I've ever eaten but extremely overpriced.
You get the point right? Good food over-priced. Great dining atmosphere, great service, a little too expensive though.
Overrated and way too expensive. If you want to show off how much money you can spend, this is a great place. If you're looking for value and taste, especially for vegetarians, look elsewhere.

This place WAS a complete dive with awesome & affordable food 12 years ago but now it's totally overpriced. It still looks the same as it did back then, the portions are huge, the food tastes good but not for the prices. My husband and I ate here yesterday and ordered chicken and oxtail entrees with 2 extra sides and no drinks. They didn't not have all the items listed on the menu and the bill was over $50! With those kind of prices you'd expect they at least  try to improve on the service and esthetics of the restaurant. I will not come back here.

Food was good - not spectacular and the price was way too high.  
Great ambiance for a casual stop in but still not worth the price.
The restaurant itself is chic, but not fancy and luxury. The food is like meh. Does NOT worth the price at all, and $$ is like the maximum you should charge

I was super excited to try this place! But honestly it is NOT worth the price. 

This place is ridiculously expensive for no reason. It's just salads and toppings. I did like that they had hot toppings but still toppings. I paid like $12 for this meal. The salad was ok.... I enjoyed the array of options but the employees weren't that friendly while making my food. 

The taste could've been more flavorful and the bread could've been moister. Ultimately, wasn't that thrilled.
Just.... Ok. I don't mind spending money on good food, but it really wasn't worth the price. Service was great.
Over priced, over hyped. Not like the food was bad, but totally not worth the price. Don't mind paying more for food you could get much better going elsewhere? - this place might be for you.

The meal was really affordable as well. 

Coming back to browse the menu some without a doubt
Great food and wonderful experience! The only issue would be the price compared to portion size-- for the appetizers. The entree portions are generous and worth the price!

They were so delicious and full of flavor and spice. 

Overall, the price point is very affordable but comes at a cost with the poor service. Would I come back again? Only if it requires a zero minute wait time.

A nice variety on the menu with very reasonable prices. Went with a group of 4 and had 3 appetizers and 4 entrees for under $20 a person including tip. Food was flavorful although no additional sauces were on the table or offered. Although there were only a few other tables with customers felt rushed during dining. Overall a decent meal.

The most overpriced and overrated restaurant in the city.
Food is uniformly mediocre.
Service is poor. A constantly changing cast of characters (servers is a  misnomer) showed they couldn't have cared less about us.
The noise level is overwhelming and conversation inhibiting.
The menu prices are far in excess in relation to the uniformly poor food served late
 Food which should have been served hot was repeatedly served warm at best.
Ingredients of dishes  were misrepresented  by bored waitpeople (i.e., malt is not vanilla).
No one working here cares about customers and a general lack of interest is constantly reinforced.
Don't bother climbing the steps to the dining room. Definitely go elsewhere (or stay home).

In brief, I recommend. The building was lovely and spacious. The food was very good, the servings were huge, and the waitstaff professional and competent. All around very good. The only thing I wanted to note specifically was this appeared in a Yelp list of "quiet restaurants near center city, Philadelphia" and--at least last night, around 6 pm--it was anything but quiet. At a table of four, I had a lot of difficulty hearing. So, if you are looking for quiet conversation, this may not be a good spot. Otherwise, go and enjoy!

Great service and interesting food that we would like to explore, however, the noise level is unsettling. We were there on a week night with place 1/3 filled and our group of 6 had a hard time hearing conversation. It's disappointing for a newly constructed facility to not have considered sound dampening aspects. Hopefully the owners can correct this.

Food and service were terrific. BBQ oysters, grilled octopus, sauteed fresh flounder. However, the loud noise ruined our dinner. My friend from NY said it was the loudest restaurant she has ever been in. Even our waitress said she had to read lips. We would not return unless they improve acoustics.

The noise level in this restaurant makes it virtually impossible to hold a conversation. Low light level made reading the menu a challenge. If you can get past those obstacles you will find the food a delight and the service efficient and friendly.
Good good, nice space- but what really stands out is how LOUD it is. I am no crotchety old woman, but when I can't hear any of the dinner conversation, that is a problem.

Place was so loud it was to the point of being startling.  Had a loud ass four top of Millennials next to us who kept shouting over each other.   We were packed into the back room when there was ample seating available upstairs which we didn't notice until we walked out.   Food was meh... Hard to eat when you're being subjected to ear torture.   Recommendation is to install some sound deadening material on the walls or tell people to shut the f*ck up.

The food is quite good, and the free chips and salsa are fresh, tasty, and plentiful.  Service is consistent, fast, and suprisingly attentive given the always rapid pace.

Did I mention the fab margarita selection?  If there are two or more of you it's definitely worth getting a pitcher... if you don't mind the buzz you'll carry out with you afterward.  Blood Orange is my fave, but I recently had the Cucumber and it was really interesting and perfect for a hot summer day.

If you've ever had tacos at a legit taqueria you will be slightly disappointed with Cantina's version, however.  Close to the real thing but not quite.  The burrito's won't set the world on fire either, but they are pretty good and you certainly get a lot of food for the price.

We just stumbled across this place while looking for somewhere to eat near our hotel. It looked cute on the outside, but it was a total circus on the inside. There is a bar, and a couple of dining areas, but unfortunately they all seemed to converge right where we were sitting, meaning that our table was constantly being pushed past by everyone, which made for a very poor, very hassled dining experience. Even worse was the ear-splitting noise. This place was so loud, my friend and I had to shout at each other across our small table, and ended up downing our drinks and packing up our food just so we could get out of there before any permanent hearing loss occurred  (hopefully).
I've been here a few times.  I think the food is good not great.   My biggest complaint is the noise level.  When the place is full it's incredibly loud and hard to have a conversation.

Positive: Mostly good food.
Negative: Holy cr@p, it is loud!  Even with the restaurant only 2/3 full, you have to scream to make the person next to you hear what you're saying.

My boyfriend and I had dinner reservations at XIX Nineteen to celebrate our anniversary. I was initially very excited to have dinner here, because of the gorgeous view and the great reviews I read online.  However, when I got there, it was anything but amazing.

When we made the reservation (almost a month ahead of time), we requested to sit near a window, but when we got to the restaurant we were told that they didn't have anything available.  That was clearly a lie, because there were multiple tables near windows in the main dining room.  Strike number one.

Our waiter seemed very nice at first.  However, when he realized we weren't spending money on appetizers or alcohol, his whole demeanor changed.  I don't expect A+ service all the time, but if we're spending $100+ at a restaurant, I want my waiter to be happy and pleased to serve us. Strike two.

My wife and I dine here this past Saturday night.  We had an early reservation, but the place was already full, both on the first floor and second floor.  Each floor has a bar with a nice selection of liquor and an outstanding selection of wines.  Service was excellent.  The menu, although limited, was creative and the food was good.  Not great, but good.  The reason for the low rating is that the noise level is extreme.  The walls, ceilings and floors are all hard surfaces, with nothing to absorb sound except for patrons' clothing.  The prices are relatively high, but I wouldn't have cared that much if the entire experience had been enjoyable -- which it wasn't.  What good is a good restaurant where you can't talk?  We will never go back.

El Vez has great guacamole and chips, the chicken tacos are delicious and the shrimp enchiladas are amazing but I will never go back because the noise level was horrendous. My husband and I had important plans to discuss but were unable to have even a simply conversation. It's so loud everyone in the restaurant is shouting including the waitresses.
The food isn't worth the noise!

A hard review to write, as i loved the food and thought that our server was fantastic. But, this was without any doubt, the single loudest restaurant that I've ever been to. It was loud enough to significantly effect my experience. 

If you are in anyway sensitive to noise or, if like me, just simply prefer a quieter atmosphere, this is by no means an option.

The food is awesome, but it is so incredibly loud there it's not a very pleasant place to eat. I came for a date with my boo, and we had to scream at each other above the din. It was hard to relax and enjoy the food, because it was impossible to have a conversation. It is pretty crowded (easy to bang elbows with your neighbor) and that doesn't help the noise sitch since you can hear them screaming as well. Maybe if I was at the bar for a lively drink it would be fun, but the care put into the food is not matched by care put into the experience of eating the food.

I've been here before. Food and margs are decent, but the noise level was UNCOMFORTABLY LOUD! I HAD TO MOVE MY CHAIR TO THE SIDE IN THE HOPES I COUKD HEAR MY DINNER COMPANION. IT DIDN'T WORK! When I asked the waiter if it was always this loud on a Friday night, he shrugged and replied, "If people are talking loudly." A trip through the restaurant to the bathroom confirmed it was loud everywhere. SO APPARENTLY PEOPLE TALK LOUD AT THE BAR, IN A DINING ROOM.... If you go, go on a warm evening and sit on the patio if you would like to have a conversation that isn't punctuated by "Huh?" and "What?".

I've been to this location a number of times, and have to agree it's been slipping in quality and service.  We went on a Friday night, and I have to say it was, hands-down, the loudest restaurant I've ever been to.  Not their fault, just what it is.  There were a number of large groups of what appeared to be students, and every one of these groups was obnoxiously loud.  Not just talking, but screaming, singing, etc.  It started to resemble a loud frat party.  The staff were working hard, and running around like lunatics trying to keep things moving.  This created a frenetic atmosphere, and both people and staff were pushing past our table, and on occasion, knocking things off the table.  It was a chaotic scene, to say the least.  We waited about 20 minutes for our reserved table.  

The food ranged from just OK to pretty good.

We ate at Zahav for the first time, but I was familiar with Solomonov's recipes from his wonderful cookbook. The incomparable braised lamb shoulder with chickpeas and pomegranate molasses glaze has been a star at three different company meals in our home. It is amazing!
   We were too late to order that this trip--they run out early--but we got the tasting menu which is just incredible. The salads, hummus, and bread are enough for a whole meal, but then come the mezzes, entrees, and desserts. Thankfully, the entrees are smaller than the mezzes! That is something I never thought I would hear myself say. The service was great. 
   My one complaint--and it is a BIG one because it kinda ruined the evening--is the phenomenally loud music being piped. We complained twice, and it got marginally better.

We were very pleased to get a lovely booth when we arrived. Our server was excellent and the food terrific. The restaurant is very attractive and inviting. However, the restaurant is SO NOISY that we had difficulty conversing and enjoying our meal. There was loud rock like music on the sound system which does not go with such a fine restaurant. In addition there were large groups nearby that added to the noise. It is unfortunate and we would never return. The Prices are VERY high. It is just not worth it.

The food was excellent, the waiter was excellent.  Our issue was with the noise level.  It was difficult for my wife and I to have a conversation.  It was a combination of the decor (hardwood floors) and the other restaurant patrons.  We we surrounded with loud-mouthed diners, who spoke far too loud.  The restaurant needs to move and not tell the current patrons where they are going.  We would go back for the food and service, but are reluctant due to the clientele.

too loud!  will not go again.  a 1:30 lunch should have been more quiet.  however, the music was blaring, to add to the noise level.  dining with friends to me means a chance to talk and eat good food.  talking was painful.  we had to shout to be heard.  and this was at a table in the front by the window.  it should have been more quiet that it was.
food can be great, but not worth the $$, in absense of ability to converse with friends.

Yes the restaurant is noisy but honestly, do you really expect to sit in a quiet restaurant on a weekend night? I did have to speak above my normal volume but I still didn't feel like I was shouting. I will definitely be back to El Vez, and soon!

Food is cool service and atmosphere is lousey. And very loud i asked to move seating twice and still a particular group of patrons was very loud with no one to ask them to quiet down a bit... the ppl who dined here that night were very upset.

When the place I wanted to go for lunch was closed, I decided to try this place.  It was great to find a restaurant with a lot of veggie-based, but not all strictly vegetarian or vegan, options.  The salad I had (Wild Child) was excellent.  The rest of the menu looks great too.  But one thing kept me from giving it 5 or even 4 stars:
WHY IS THE MUSIC SO LOUD!!!!?

I like music.  In fact, I love music.  I play music. I go to music events.  I have accepted that no restaurant can tolerate, or thinks its customers can tolerate, a quiet background.  So, there's music. But this was so loud it made me feel anxious and rush my meal. Is that what restaurant management wants?  There's no need in this case, because it wasn't at all crowded, I could have lingered and relaxed without a tiny bit of guilt over making others wait for a table.  But yet I couldn't, because it was too loud.

A quiet Sunday dinner???- NOT AT FORK. Why? Crowded? No-half empty. Loud guests? No. Sound system volume excessive? YES. Polite request x 3 to turn it down ignored despite complaints from other patron(s). If you like to shout at your companion for the entire dinner due to the overly loud music, this is the place.

While the food and service were quite good, there are numerous other establishments that provide fine food and an ambiance that does not reflect the arrogance of the establishment.

Been several times as it is by my house and has big tables that are easy to work at.  But, I am thinking of not going back.  Its constantly very loud inside and the manager / owner is rude.  Most of the other staff is nice, albeit one of them is constantly talking loud behind the counter and is just obnoxious.  Would like it more if it was a little more quite and peaceful to work at.
Great atmosphere, food and drinks. We were sitting upstairs and it was really quiet which was great cause we could easily talk. Everyone was really nice to us, no complaints
So disappointed! Certainly not a quiet place for conversation and enjoying those you're with. The volume of music and loud talk really made me dislike the food. Would not hurry to go back.

Tried this place for the first time. The noise levels absolutely ruined the experience for us and it was supppsed to be a special birthday night! Not a place to come for a quiet date night or even if you just want to have a conversation with someone. There was so much noise with the party next to us, it ruined this experience for us. The waitress was sympathetic and the food was yummy, but I'll think twice before coming back here. The noise was really that bad folks!

Heard this place was good so why not give it a try. Came here last night for a friends birthday. 

Noise level was extremely loud that my friends and I couldn't hear each other talking. Our server was yelling as she was explaining the menu to us. If you want a nice quiet dinner, this place is definitely not it. If you want to scream at each other during dinner then this is the place.

Our server was very rude and kept messing up our order. When we told her we didn't order these food items she said my friends and I didn't communicate correctly because she heard someone order this.. when the food got to our table we all claim our entree but there were 4 extra items that we did not order. The server kept saying someone ordered this and we should figure out who ordered what and not blame the server. She mention it was her job to take orders, not figure out who ordered what.

All in all good food but vastly overrated given the hype. I might have guessed...but still. And I do have two MAJOR complaints. 
One waitress, the head person in the dining room,  is so obnoxiously loud that I could almost not finish my meal. She stood next to our table bellowing out comments on the food to the table right next ours (I suspect it is the person who reviewed below), a couple of self-professed foodies who kept asking her about every dish. She came back at least four times, each time for a ten minute conversation--thereby ignoring the rest of her guests. Aside from the fact that her butt was facing me most of that time (as in ten inches away from my head), the volume and inanity started to seriously get on my nerves. All the more annoying that this was delightfully quiet dining room. Excessive noise, especially in a high end place, is one of my pet peeves.

Reserved for two at 6 PM. Wanted as much quiet as Vernick could provide. On arrival told the lovely hostess the same and she seated at a pleasant table in the room adjacent to the kitchen. Looked like a fine spot and during the first first course or two the ambient sound remained reasonably quiet. However once things warmed up in the adjacent bar area, a dull roar of people noise took over making it literally impossible to have a conversation with my dinner partner.  

Of course everything we value in fine dining was present in spades. The food was incredible and the service excellent. Too bad the sound diminished the pleasure of the occasion. 

Vernick: you need an accoustical redo of your space!! But otherwise  don't change a thing.

The food was good particularly the kale salad and the steak, but what got me was the noise of the music and the conversation of many others to the detriment of my being able to hear the person across the table from me. If I go out to a restaurant, I think the least the establishment can do is provide me a place to be able to communicate with fellow dinners. The dessert was so small as to be....a taste of a cake and fig ice cream. I will not go back.
I think they should investigate improving the acoustics of the space. There are too many hard surfaces and nothing to deaden the sounds.
The food was great except that there is not much room inside the restaurant I guess the reason is because they serve a very sumptuous meal that's why it's always crowded.

This was one of the best meals I had during the 4 years I went to school in Philly.  I saved it for my senior year, and it was well worth the wait.  The service was impeccable, and the food itself was amazing.  I was temporarily overwhelmed by the variety and couldn't decide if I wanted to take the sweet or savory brunch route.  Luckily the buffet setup allows you to do a little of both.

The place was a little more quiet and formal than I'm usually comfortable with, but who cares when you have such a great brunch spread before you?

I like this little joint for their delicious coffee and amazing service, but I hate that they allow about 15-20 people in this very small space. It's definitely beyond full capacity because all the tables are full and people waiting in line inside from the bathroom area to the other side of the entrance. It's SCARY because that's definitely putting people in danger.

I've only been here for brunch but it is one of my go-to places to eat on a weekend. I've had several of their brunch meals but always with a side of sausage. I don't normally order a side of sausage but it is that good. Recently I had their 9-grain pancakes with bananas. I was pleasantly surprised when I received the pancakes and the bananas were cooked into the pancake - score! Everything I've ever gotten there is fresh and tasty. I really enjoy the bread basket that includes cornbread, rye, and some other yummy slices and jelly. Depending on who is paying I would advise getting a mimosa. I word it that way because I think they are too expensive but very tasty. 

Overall I love this place. I can always expect fresh and tasty food. I also can always expect a wait (on the weekends for brunch). I've found that if you arrive at 10:45 or earlier you don't have too long of a wait.

When you're walking around the tourist area of Philly and get a rumble in your stomach, what do you do? You could go for some Italian food, which there is plenty of in Philly, but you can also go for a Philly Cheese steak. AND, when your wife has NEVER HAD a Philly Cheese steak, you have to make her first experience memorable.

This is where Oh Brother comes into the picture. It's close enough from the tourist sites to walk, and the food is on point!

The menu has a good selection of sandwiches, burgers and milkshakes. There are also vegetarian options if you're into that.

The wife and I both went for the cheese steaks with Whiz and shared an order of sweet potato fries. Although, admittedly, all the fries looked good and I'm sure you'll be happy regardless of which option you get.

I used to love coming here for date night, but now it feels like they overbook shows and understaff for service. I came in here tonight with my husband and we got seated at a small shared table with another couple, with not enough space for food and drinks so that I had to hold my drink on my lap the whole time. On top of that, it felt like we were intruding on the other couple's date because I was sitting closer to them than my husband.  When we asked to be moved to another table, we were told that they were sold out and didn't have any other tables available (even though there were many visible since we arrived early). They also did not have nearly enough staff; we were seated for 30 minutes before anyone approached us for food or drink orders (and it was only because I had to get up and flag someone over), which was ridiculous. I don't think I would come back here in the near future.

Came here once for dinner with my girlfriends. The food was very good and the ambiance is super cute, but we felt like we were being rushed out of the place for no reason. There were plenty of open tables and no one waiting to sit, so I didn't quite understand that. If they are more patient with their patrons I might come back.

Food is decent; but is very slow to make it to the table. 
Servers are pleasant; but are very slow and they are terribly understaffed. 
Every time I come here (out of convenience), I am underwhelmed. The space shouldn't be able to hold as many people as it does, if they are so understaffed. 
The menus are print out paper and are written on and/or torn. I'd be embarrassed to hand them to customers if I were part of the staff. 
If you make the unwise choice to come. Make a reservation and expect to be there for well over 2 hours.

Food is excellent 
Staff is friendly and very helpful
My only issue is the lack of space to sit indoors
The place gets busy at dinner time 
They are closed in Sunday's

Tight seating and BYOB, but otherwise a great experience. Everything we ordered was delicious, and the service was perfect.

The crowd appears to be a bit older, but that might have just been because we had 5:30 reservations.

I just ate here for the first time this afternoon for a late lunch. It wasn't that busy, and there wasn't anyone at the front to greet me or other customers who came in. After about a minute, I was told I could "just sit anywhere." I ended up being asked later to move to a smaller table (which was no big deal, but maybe don't tell your customers to "sit anywhere" when that may not be the case...also, other customers who came in after were greeted and taken to a table). The food didn't take long to come out and it was decent. I got three different tacos (chicken, steak, and pork) and used a couple of the hot sauces they brought out. Not amazing, but good, especially for the price. However, it took forever for the wait person to bring me my check...like at least 15-20 minutes AFTER I finished eating.

This review is more heavy on the environment of the dining experience that I had. Please be aware there is no social distancing. We walked in around 4pm and since its off hour there werent many people at first. We sat down with one empty table between us and another table in the same row which was fine; however as more parties entered the restaurant, the servers sat everyone to one side of the restaurant with no open table separating the parties while the other half was completely unoccupied and that made me feel very uncomfortable. It made the whole dinning experience unpleasant. I should've said something to the workers but at that point I just wanted to leave as soon as we could. In addition, we sat near the front counter and several workers stood behind nearby and I could hear them talk and laugh.

We had a truly horrible experience here with a group of about 10-11 people. We had called ahead, made a reservation, and throughout our meal there were never more than 1-2 other tables (with no more than two or four people at any given time). After taking quite some time to take our order, the waiter brought out 1-2 items about every 20 minutes after doing so. In other words, a meal or appetizer for only one or two people would be brought out at a time while others had not yet received any food and were forced to just sit there. This continued on throughout the whole meal.  Several members in our party entirely finished their meals while others still had not yet received an appetizer or any part of their meals.  It was very odd and frustrating.

it is a small tiny pale room with sparse decor.
the tables are jammmed in very tightly.
it is loud and not comfortable. 

food:

apps -
grilled octopus, with fingerling potatoes, and a tomato spread a+. very very meaty and not rubbery and very good. 

pumpkin gnochi  in a brown butter sauce. a +. creamy and good.

potato leak soup was flavorless. surprising since the pumpkin market has done a mean potato sunchoke soup in the past. 

entrees -

grouper w/ shrimp. oh boy. grouper was great , but the shrimp were so so salty. :*( no good. 

hanger steak. tiny strips. not really super special. 

char (like a salmon) ok. on a bed of lentils that could have been cooked 2 minutes longer.

 

desert-

pumpkin bread. dry.

coffee ice cream yum.


the waiters barely talked to us, and we really felt like we were in their way.

White Dog is not a place for a gastronomically mind-blowing experience. 

It's a good place for a fancy-ish business lunch where you want to 1) appear like you're taking someone to a fancy restaurant, 2) spend someone else's money because the food is too pricey for its value, and 3) be in good company so you can focus more on talking to your guests than on the mediocre food. 

Don't get me wrong, I love the concept of using locally sourced ingredients and the quaint atmosphere. The service is also pretty decent. But when you're a restaurant, food preparation is kind of a big deal. 

The NY Strip ($32), ordered medium-rare, came out well-done. The cut was too thick, too dry, and chewy. You need an extremely sharp knife to pierce through the rubbery surface of this really tough, unmarinated slab of meat.

We left shortly after we were seated because we quickly realized we wouldn't have an enjoyable time here, so this review is focused on the atmosphere. 

- It's kitchsy. Sure, the flowers and color scheme is fun. It's great for the 'gram. 
- It's LOUD. Like have-to-yell-to-be-heard-by-someone-sitting-across-from-you loud.  
- It's a super young crowd. Mostly all women. 
- The tables are squished together. I am a small person, and I could barely fit between the tables.
- We had a reservation, but don't even attempt to come here without one. They just turn you away.

This place has great potential and definitely has wonderful food.  Where it falls short is in regard to the ambiance and very real smallness of the place.  It is tough to be comfortable in the hard cushioned chairs and low tables, and though this may seem trivial, imagine enjoying a meal and trying to sit comfortably, while needing to move your chair in as far as it can go any time someone needs to squeeze by your table.

Waitress was nice. Food was terribly salty!
Should have sent it back but didn't. Very uncomfortably tight with seating. Staff and customers have to literally walk sideways to get thru the restaurant. Most people at the counter sat way out in the aisle. Get rid of some of the seating and make it more comfortable...please!

My partner and I were greatly excited to try the food  here. I found it unprofessional and pretentious that this restaurant turned us away because there was a large group of people but half the tables were empty. They said we would have to wait until the large group was finished eating to be seated. It was obvious with this explanation that the group had not bought out the restaurant for night and this was therefore an unacceptable way to treat a customer.

I had high expectations going here.  I walk by this place often and see lots of people eating and having a good time.  However, I was very disappointed with this place for two reasons: 1) my food was terrible; 2) the seating arrangement is awful.  

Allow me to elaborate: 1) I ordered the veggie burger and was surprised to find that the buns are the most substantial part of the dish.  Inside of two gigantic buns was a very small portobello mushroom, some sloppy grilled onions, really large pieces of lettuce, and one sliver of a zucchini.  The burger was bland and the fries that came with the burger were very salty.  I realize that this restaurant isn't known for their veggie burger, but I finished my burger and thought aloud, "I wish I could've had a veggie Whopper."  This was the worst burger I've ever had in my life.

2) the seating arrangement is a joke.

Excellent friendly staff.  I go there every day.  My only beef is with my fellow customers who think it's fine to take up two or three seats with their bags and coats  some don't even purchase anything and management doesn't seem to mind that regulars can't get a chair or outlet.

Surprise! Came here as a random indulgent desire for AYCE, it was perfect because I was starving, lol. We were greeted at the door and seated right away. Covid restrictions in place, each employee had their mask and tables were spacious to abide to regulations. Our waiter had a heavy accent, I didn't understand him well, but didn't care much because I just wanted to start eating. 

Atmosphere: Clean, had a ranch vibe with a winery feel, there was a private room that held most of the wine bottles. Spacious and great atmosphere not too cluttered like what I was used to. Green and red flip coasters were placed and red obviously meant stop and green to just keeeeeep it coming. I think I had to pause (red tab) it maybe twice toward the beginning. 

Service: Reasons for the 3 stars...  because service is a big part of experience.

A delightful venue with a far to table feel.  The service and delight were the highlights of the night, but the food fell a bit short.

**Tip, reservations are a must, even during not so busy times.  Don't just wolly (wall-e) on in.

#Location: On a busier Philly night, you might find yourself searching a hour for metered street parking, and subsequently miss your reservation, if you come during not so busy times in the middle of the week, there should be plenty of spots available.  

#Space and decor: Vernick houses a two story venue.  Downstairs is a nice and spacious bar.  Seating on the first floor (which I would have opted for if I had known about this) is in the back. Dimly lit but with clear view of the open kitchen and chefs.  We were seated up stairs which opens up to a spacious rustic room with large windows overlooking the street below.  Not really a bad seat in the house.

For this Point Breeze resident who just had a baby, this place is a savior. My wife come here every week for a few hours to decompress. We are so grateful for this spot. This is a very cool, very spacious, kid-friendly, brewery restaurant with an open, light and very uplifting atmosphere. I really like the vibes here, and the staff is super cool. I really like the feel of the cafe/brewery mix. The beer hall style tables are great for big groups, or to mingle with the local community. Every time I come here, there are several large groups hanging out. One time there was an engagement party, which I think is ideal for venue. There was a sizable engagement party and still plenty of space for public patrons. 

The food menu is probably not what most people would expect from a brewery.

Upstairs is large and spacious and the music is fun.
Two bars offer you selection on either side.
There is also allegedly food here but I never had the gumption to try with all the other Philadelphia restaurants worth trying out.

The dancefloor upstairs is spacious and the crowd is fun.
It's larger upstairs than I expected.
The restaurant was not crowded, so I wasn't understanding why the food was cold or why it took so long. While the free appetizer was appreciated, this was truly a unpleasant customer experience.

I've come here twice in the past month, once for lunch (ended up taking the food to go because there was no space) and another time for a drink. 

The space is tiny here, it's more enjoyable when it's not crowded. When ordering for lunch, it was awkward waiting for the order because there really isn't much room to stand without being in someone's way. I ordered the breakfast wrap but my two friends also ordered food that needed to be toasted and it took too long. The wrap itself was good, but really small....look how big my cookie was next to the burrito! The second time I came back, I was pretty sick and asked for a hot water but treated my friend to a drink here. Got a really weird look when they asked me if I was really ordering a hot water...I would rather go somewhere else in the area for a sandwich or drink in the future.

So, this place is cute. It's tiny, somewhat trendy with an average menu. The reason why this place has three stars is because I felt that the customer service was extremely lacking. 

After coming in, the hostess attempted to sit us in a really tiny side seat and we requested a different spot. The hostess then informs us that this isn't a place where you can just sit anywhere.
